# Pitex 2.2.0 — Release Notes

## What changed
- **New embedded editing preview** (TeXpresso/XeTeX-derived engine): a
  whole-document preview that refreshes while you edit, without saving. The
  established pdflatex / xelatex / lualatex / latexmk paths remain separate
  and unchanged. For local projects on macOS and Ubuntu 24.04 it is the
  default and replaces the compiler's live-compile path; remote (SSH)
  projects and the Ubuntu 22.04 package keep the compiler backend.
- **The macOS PDF preview remains PDFKit's PDFView.**
- **Equation hover preview** and a **multi-line compose box** (below).
- **The preview's status no longer moves the PDF.** "Updating editing
  preview…" and the error rows are now an overlay at the top of the PDF
  view; in narrow panes the SyncTeX status message is shortened to one line
  (the full text is in its tooltip and is its accessibility label).
- **The preview restarts after a build-target change.** After you open a
  file that your main document does not include (or pin / unpin the main
  document) and come back, the editing preview returns without an edit. It
  is designed not to replace the PDF of a manual Build with an editing
  preview (verified by code reading only; see Known limitations).
- **Fewer redundant updates.** A save or a disk event that changes nothing
  the preview engine could see no longer triggers an update, and an
  access-time-only file event on an open file no longer makes the app re-read
  it in a loop (macOS; the same file-watching code is in 2.1.6, not observed
  there).
- **Preview updates (macOS):** while a new PDF is drawn, the previous page image is kept on screen (for up to about a second; see Known limitations).
- **Equation preview fixes:** a formula that fits no longer shows both
  scrollbars; a preview that follows another one that was just hidden is now
  shown.

### Live-compile behaviour
- These live-compile changes apply to the compiler backend. Live builds use
  a fixed coalescing window from the first edit ("Build delay", default
  700 ms).
- A running live build now finishes instead of being cancelled; newer edits
  coalesce into one follow-up build.
- Changing the build context (including the resolved main document) retires
  live work.
- The Build delay setting applies only to the Compiler compatibility preview (default 700 ms); the embedded editing preview uses a fixed 100 ms delay.
- Setting descriptions updated in all shared locales.

## Known limitations / unverified
- **Preview swap (macOS):** while the preview updates it can show the
  previous page image for up to about a second (the cap), and the
  forward-search highlight can appear only after that. The preview keeps the
  previous page image on screen until the new page has been drawn. No automated in-app
  check of this change was run, the maintainer did not check the release
  build, and there was no observation on a physical display. A margin of 50 ms after PDFKit draws is a heuristic; there is no
  setting for this behaviour.
- **What was checked in-app:** the file-watcher and update-filter changes
  (macOS) were checked in-app on a pre-release build; the final build adds
  the restart-after-target-change and swap-cover changes and was not re-run
  in-app. The release build was not checked by the maintainer either (his
  decision of 2026-10-04). The
  restart-after-target-change change: no automated in-app check; reviewed in
  code; its protection of a built PDF is verified by code reading only. Two
  limits: an edit made within about 100 ms before the preview session starts
  shows only with the next edit; after the restart the built PDF from disk
  is shown for about 350 ms until the restarted preview publishes.
- **Linux:** CI tests only; not verified on a Linux desktop. The Ubuntu 22.04
  package uses the compiler backend.
- **PDFKit console warning:** "Drawing a PDFPage when its PDFDocument is nil
  is unsupported." appeared on macOS 26.5.2 in automated runs (2 of 5
  processes in the measured control); 0 target lines in 5 runs (10 app-process logs) on macOS 27.0.1, exposure not verified, which is weak evidence. macOS 15 is
  not tested. This release does not claim to fix it.
- The equation-preview acceptance run (N5) has not passed; its last run
  stopped at a checker defect on a Korean-language host (the checker's comparison was corrected in C29, not re-run); the assistant-font check could not run (a checker defect already
  on `main`).
- Caret/last-line visibility immediately after a bulk paste: open
  (human check pending).
- macOS 15 (the app's minimum) was not tested at runtime.
- Hosted CI: the release workflow builds and checks the DMG, the Ubuntu
  packages, the helpers and the AppArmor proof before it publishes — see the
  PR for the run result.
- Ubuntu 24.04: the deb installs an AppArmor profile,
  `/etc/apparmor.d/pitex`, so WebKit's sandbox (used by the equation preview)
  can start where Ubuntu restricts user namespaces. This was checked on a
  GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04 runner with the restriction on, not on a desktop
  install. The Ubuntu 22.04 deb installs no profile. Upgrading from 2.1.6
  installs the profile.
- Linux: not natively verified. (Windows is excluded from 2.2.0 — see
  "Windows" below.)

## Windows
Windows: there is no Windows download for 2.2.0, and the Windows downloads
of earlier releases have been removed. Existing Windows installations keep
working; their in-app update check will report that no suitable download is
available. These downloads were removed on 2026-10-02. Windows (beta)
support will return in a later release.

## Licensing
2.2.0 adds third-party components:
- **Preview engine:** TeXpresso (MIT), XeTeX, Tectonic (MIT); TECkit
  LGPL-2.1-or-later, unmodified and dynamically linked — see
  `PreviewEngine/licenses/`.
- **MathJax 4** (Apache-2.0), bundled offline for the equation preview.
The app bundles no third-party PDF viewer code.

## Equation hover preview
- Hovering an equation, or moving the caret into one, shows a rendered
  preview above or below it without building the document (macOS; Linux with
  WebKitGTK 6.0).
- Math detection for inline/display delimiters and math environments, with
  TeX-faithful handling of comments, escapes, verbatim and `\text`, plus
  document-order user macros.
- Fast preview via bundled offline MathJax 4 (TeX font, SVG) in a sandboxed
  web view with a render watchdog and bounded automatic recovery.
- Exact TeX preview (Build > Exact Equation Preview, ⌥⌘E / Ctrl+Alt+E)
  compiles only the equation with the project's preamble and engine in a
  private temporary folder, with optional automatic fallback.
- Settings > Editor > Equation Preview, in all shared locales.

## Multi-line compose box
- Multi-line input field fixed; the composer grows up to 8 lines then scrolls.
- Return sends; ⌥Return inserts a newline; Shift+Return also sends.
- Cmd+Return in the field does nothing (observed); the Send button's
  shortcut code is unchanged (not exercised at app level).

## Scope of proof

Compose box — verbatim from its acceptance report:
- **Proves:** this exact modifier chain grows to 8 lines then scrolls, and the
  key behaviour is as asserted, on macOS 27.0.1 (26A434), Apple M4, built
  against the macOS SDK reported by the precondition step (must print 27.x —
  otherwise STOP; do not claim a specific SDK until shown).
- **Does not prove:** the Pitex app integration; real IME; trackpad scrolling;
  VoiceOver; **macOS 15.0 (the deployment floor) or 26.x**; builds with other
  SDKs or the release toolchain; Debug vs Release differences.
- Open for release: app-level verification on macOS 15.0 / 26.x unverified.

Embedded preview — verbatim from the frozen evidence scope:
- Evidence produced on a macOS 26.5.2 virtual machine (Xcode 27.0 RC). The
  release-payload audit inspected a Release `Pitex.app` built there (helpers
  built on the VM, not by the release pipeline); the other checks used
  checker-built apps.

## How the preview-engine helpers were tested
The preview-engine helpers in this release are built by the release
pipeline on macOS 15. The automated tests described above used a
separately built set of helpers that also contained the GLib, libintl
and PCRE2 libraries; those libraries are not part of the released
helpers. A later round on a physical Mac mini (macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0)
audited the CI-built DMG of an earlier head of this release (no pdf.js, helpers
equal to the CI payload and targeting macOS 15.0, no GLib / libintl / PCRE2,
strict ad-hoc code signature, no notarization) and ran the layout, SyncTeX,
workspace and release checks on a Release build with those helpers; the
embedded-preview checker fully passed in 2 of 5 runs, the other 3 stopped at the stale-SyncTeX step because the preview had already caught up when the check looked (counted as checker timing, not as passes). Commits after that head were not
re-run in that setup.
## Verification ledger
Verification logged 69 process and record issues (as of 2026-10-04); each one's effect on the results is listed in the pull request.
